title: Prefer structured JSON before DOM rows for SPA extraction
summary: After authorized observation of an authenticated SPA, content-filtered same-origin JSON payloads are often a safer extraction source than brittle DOM rows; keep per-item source telemetry and an explicit DOM fallback.
ai_value: Helps agents build extraction tools that are stable, observable, and auth-safe without overfitting to transient DOM or opaque endpoint names.

contexts: an authenticated SPA renders identifiers or records from same-origin JSON payloads
DOM rows are virtualized, translated, reordered, or incomplete
the extraction must remain within an already authorized observation session

trigger_signals.description: DOM selectors can find visible rows but miss stable identifiers, hidden fields, or pagination state.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Inspect captured same-origin JSON payload shapes before committing to DOM scraping.

trigger_signals.description: Endpoint names are opaque, unstable, or shared by multiple payload types.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Filter by content shape and required fields, not just URL substrings.

trigger_signals.description: Extracted items lack source-field or missing-reason telemetry.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Add per-item telemetry so extraction drift becomes visible.

negative_signals.description: Using network payloads would require bypassing authentication or accessing data outside the authorized UI session.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: Do not broaden access; stay within the authorized observation boundary.

negative_signals.description: The DOM is the contractual source and JSON payloads are intentionally incomplete or unstable.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: Then DOM extraction with stronger assertions may be the safer contract.

common_wrong_assumptions: The visible DOM is always the safest extraction source.
Endpoint URL names are reliable enough filters for SPA payloads.
Missing identifiers can be silently skipped if most rows extract.

first_checks.check: Capture authorized same-origin JSON payloads and identify content-shape predicates for the needed records.
first_checks.why: Content shape is often more stable than endpoint names or DOM layout.

first_checks.check: Add parser tests for primary payload, fallback payload, missing identifier, and DOM fallback cases.
first_checks.why: Tests keep extraction failures observable as the SPA evolves.

first_checks.check: Emit per-item source-field and missing-reason telemetry.
first_checks.why: Telemetry distinguishes no data from extraction drift.

decision_rules.condition: Authorized structured payloads contain the needed identifiers and fields.
decision_rules.then: Use content-shape predicates to parse JSON before falling back to DOM rows.

decision_rules.condition: Structured payloads are absent or outside the authorized session.
decision_rules.then: Use the DOM path and record the absence reason rather than bypassing authentication.

decision_rules.condition: Telemetry shows missing identifiers or fallback spikes.
decision_rules.then: Inspect payload shape and DOM changes before trusting partial results.

do_not: Do not bypass authentication or broaden data access to obtain JSON.
Do not filter only by opaque endpoint names when content shape is available.
Do not silently drop items with missing identifiers.
Do not apply extraction guidance to browser mutations; cross-check admin-form-writers-need-warmup-and-readback when the task writes remote admin state.

agent_directives.preferred_next_step: In an authorized SPA session, inspect same-origin JSON payload shapes, add parser/fallback tests, and emit per-item source telemetry.

risk.notes: This record is de-identified agent guidance. It does not authorize bypassing maintainer, security, publication, production, billing, data, permission, or destructive-action gates.

sources.supports: candidate note 31 was selected as a standalone browser extraction record and cross-linked to admin form writer discipline.
